sections.section_title: The First Beast Rises from the Sea
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the beast's emergence from the sea with ten horns and seven heads, receiving its power, throne, and authority from the dragon; the section establishes the beast's identity and origin rather than addressing the believer's standing.

sections.section_title: The Healed Wound and the Worship of the Beast
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the beast's healed mortal wound as a parody of the Lamb's death and resurrection, and the earth-dwellers' resulting worship of the dragon and beast; the section establishes the false worship system rather than directly addressing the believer's standing.

The neutral reading describes the beast's forty-two months of blasphemous authority against God, his name, his dwelling, and those who dwell in heaven; the section characterizes the beast's hostility rather than addressing the believer's standing.

sections.section_title: The Beast's War and Universal Authority
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the beast's authority to make war on and overcome the saints, alongside the statement that all earth-dwellers whose names have not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb will worship the beast.
sections.relevance: The phrase 'whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been slain' implies pre-temporal divine registration of God's people. The neutral reading notes that 17:8 unambiguously attaches 'from the foundation of the world' to the writing of names, and that the text functions pastorally as assurance that the faithful 'are not newly or tenuously inscribed but have been in God's register since the beginning.' The beast's power has a hard boundary: it cannot compel worship from those in the Lamb's book. This implies a permanence to divine registration. However, the neutral reading also notes the paradox that the beast 'overcomes' the saints physically while the saints overcome spiritually (12:11), and 3:5 threatens name-blotting, introducing ambiguity about whether registration is unconditional.
key_phrases: everyone whose name has not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb who has been slain
it was given to him to make war with the saints and to overcome them

sections.summary: The neutral reading identifies this as a direct address to the assemblies, calling for perseverance and faith as the defining characteristics of the saints in the face of the beast's devastating authority.
sections.relevance: The phrase 'Here is the perseverance and the faith of the saints' defines sainthood by two ongoing qualities: hypomonē (patient endurance, the sustained refusal to capitulate) and pistis (faith/faithfulness, trust in God). The neutral reading notes that hypomonē 'is not passive resignation but active, resolute endurance' and that faith specifies its character as 'confidence that the bounded period will end, that the Lamb's victory is real, that the book of life is secure.' The passage implies that the saints' identity is constituted by ongoing endurance and trust, not merely by an initial event.
key_phrases: Here is the perseverance and the faith of the saints
If anyone has an ear, let him hear

sections.section_title: The Second Beast Rises from the Earth
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the second beast as a lamb-like figure that speaks like the dragon and exercises the first beast's authority to compel worship; the section establishes the false prophet's identity and function rather than directly addressing the believer's standing.

sections.section_title: Signs, the Image, and the Breath of Life
sections.summary: The neutral reading describes the false prophet's counterfeit signs, the construction and animation of the beast's image, and the death penalty for refusal to worship the image; the section establishes the coercive apparatus of the beast system.

The neutral reading describes the universal imposition of the beast's mark on right hand or forehead as a prerequisite for economic participation, creating a binary choice between compliance and exclusion.
sections.relevance: The mark system forces a binary allegiance choice on every person. The neutral reading's entire framework of two competing marks (the divine name of 14:1 versus the beast's mark of 13:16-17), two competing foreheads, and two competing identities implies that allegiance is an ongoing choice with real consequences. Those who take the mark face the third angel's warning (14:9-11); those who refuse face economic exclusion and death (13:15, 17). The binary structure implies that one's standing before God is determined by maintained allegiance -- a conditional framework.
key_phrases: he causes all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free men and the slaves, to be given a mark
no one will be able to buy or to sell, except the one who has the mark

sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the gematria puzzle of the beast's number (666) as a call for wisdom and discernment; the section is an identification riddle rather than a statement about the believer's standing.
